assets.identity_finding: Kraken publishes the asset as Infinity Ground on BNB Chain, and both its asset page and its 2025-11-04 listing notice state that Infinity Ground (AIN) makes decentralized app creation accessible through AI-powered no-code tools, that its agentic IDE lets users build dApps via natural language, and that the AIN token powers fees, payments and governance. Independently, Infinity Ground's own whitepaper publishes the [AIN] token as the lifeblood of Infinity Ground, serving as the payment token for services and transaction fees, membership and launchpad access, governance participation and staking -- the same product and the same three named utilities. Both organisations therefore agree on ticker, project and token role. DISCLOSED LIMIT: the project's own whitepaper never states a blockchain or a contract address, and its website and blog both refuse automated capture, so no exact-contract claim is made and the BNB Chain representation is Kraken's listing alone rather than a two-source chain agreement. This is the same shape as the ratified ZIG record, where the project publishes tokenomics and Kraken supplies the listed representation; it is recorded conservatively and the test pins the disclosure so it cannot later be read as a project-confirmed chain or contract claim.

Kraken publishes the asset as Bio Protocol on Solana. Independently, Bio Protocol's own documentation states that BIO is the native token of Bio Protocol and publishes its Basic Token Information page listing BIO on Solana with token contract bioJ9JTqW62MLz7UKHU69gtKhPpGi1BQhccj2kmSvUJ, together with the Ethereum contract and the BNB representation and a 3,320,000,000 starting supply. Both organisations agree on ticker, chain and project, and the record binds the published Solana mint, which is the representation Kraken lists.

Kraken publishes the asset as Brazilian Real on Polygon. Independently, the BRL1 issuer's own site describes BRL1 as a stablecoin that brings the Brazilian Real to the digital economy, backed 1:1 with total transparency by reserves of government bonds held in financial institutions with regular external certification, states that BRL1 has been natively implemented on Polygon with planned expansion to other blockchains and interoperability with PIX, publishes its audited Proof of Reserves and audited token contract 0x5c067c80c00ecd2345b05e83a3e758ef799c40b5, and names the issuing consortium. Both organisations agree on ticker, chain and the fiat-pegged nature of the asset. The verdict is therefore the excluded category stablecoin rather than eligible_crypto, on the same basis as the ratified AUSD record: this is a source-coverage classification, not an investability claim.

Kraken publishes the asset as Clearpool on Ethereum (ERC-20). Independently, Clearpool's own documentation publishes a token page giving Ticker CPOOL, Type ERC20, Initial Total Supply 1,000,000,000 and Contract (Ethereum) 0x66761fa41377003622aee3c7675fc7b5c1c2fac5, alongside its Solana, Polygon and Mantle representations. Both organisations agree on ticker, chain and token standard, and the record binds the Ethereum contract, which is the representation Kraken lists.

Kraken publishes the asset as Katana on the Katana network. Independently, Katana's own blog post announces that the network is Katana and the token is KAT with a 10b KAT supply minted, and Katana's own technical contract-address reference lists the asset KAT at 0x7f1f4b4b29f5058fa32cc7a97141b8d7e5abdc2d with origin Native, i.e. issued on the Katana chain itself rather than bridged. Both organisations agree on ticker, chain and project, and the record binds the published contract. DISAMBIGUATION: KAT is Katana's governance and incentive asset, not the chain's gas token, and is distinct from the vKAT and avKAT staking derivatives published on the same page.

Kraken publishes the asset as Sonic on the Sonic network, the project's own chain. Independently, Sonic Labs' own S Token page states that S powers the network and that the native token of the Sonic network has multiple functions including governance, staking and fee generation. Both organisations agree on ticker, chain and project. This is a native-coin identity on the project's own layer-1, the same source shape as the ratified ETC and VET native-coin records, so there is no contract address to bind and none is claimed.

Kraken publishes the asset as STBL on BNB Chain. Independently, STBL's own developer documentation publishes a Deployed Contracts table whose BNB Smart Chain Mainnet - 56 (0x38) section lists STBL_Token at 0x8dEdf84656fa932157e27C060D8613824e7979e3, and the project's own FAQ publishes the official contract addresses for its separate USST stablecoin on Ethereum, Stellar and BNB Chain. Both organisations agree on ticker and chain, and the record binds the published BNB Chain contract. DISAMBIGUATION, and the reason the verdict is eligible_crypto rather than stablecoin: the project's own documentation separates the two tokens explicitly -- USST is the over-collateralised, dollar-pegged stablecoin, while STBL is the governance and value-capture token layered on top of it through staking, buybacks and voting. The ticker also collides with an unrelated stbl.io precious-metals project; the BNB Chain contract is what ties Kraken's listing to the stbl.com Stablecoin 2.0 project rather than to that one.

Kraken publishes the asset as SuperVerse on Ethereum (ERC-20). Independently, SuperVerse's own documentation states that there is NO new Token, that $SUPER ERC20 remains THE token of the SuperVerse and that existing SUPER holders need not touch their assets, links the token's Ethereum contract 0xe53ec727dbdeb9e2d5456c3be40cff031ab40a55, and warns readers to follow only official sources while naming and branding are updated across exchanges and explorers. Both organisations agree on ticker, chain and token standard, and the record binds the published contract; the project's own no-new-token statement is what rules out a migration having moved this ticker.

Kraken publishes the asset as Tac with the network field blank, which on its face gives nothing to match. Kraken's own listing notice of 2025-07-15 resolves that: it states TAC is a purpose-built blockchain that enables EVM dApps to tap into the TON and Telegram user base of over one billion users and brings EVM compatibility and liquidity to the TON ecosystem. Independently, TAC Protocol's own blog publishes that $TAC is the exclusive gas token for executing transactions and smart contracts on the TAC EVM and that TAC extends The Open Network's DeFi ecosystem to Telegram's user base. Both organisations therefore describe the same TON-integrated EVM layer-1 and the same native token, which is what disambiguates this listing from the unrelated tokens that also trade as TAC. This is a native gas-coin identity on the project's own chain, so Kraken's blank network is correct rather than missing, there is no contract address to bind and none is claimed.

Kraken publishes the asset as XMoney on Sui. Independently, xMoney's own token page publishes Token Symbol XMN, Max Supply 10,000,000,000 and the Sui Contract Address ($XMN) 0x97c7571f4406cdd7a95f3027075ab80d3e9c937c2a567690d31e14ab1872ccee, alongside a separate MultiversX ESDT identifier for the same ticker. Both organisations agree on ticker and chain, and the record binds the published Sui object address, which is the representation Kraken lists.

scope: Source-coverage universe identity only: not investability, not capacity, not venue selection, not candidate promotion, not Regime activation, not Production wiring, not trading authority.
verification_bar: Two independent official sources per asset: the retained Kraken catalog (enabled asset with exactly one online <ASSET>/USD pair) plus Kraken's published asset name and network, matched independently against a project/foundation protocol document, token contract publication, migration notice or exact-contract asset report. Ticker text alone was not accepted. Kraken's own metadata carries no chain, contract or genesis field, so Kraken alone never satisfies the bar. Where the project publishes an exact contract or mint the record binds that identifier; where it publishes only the chain and token standard the record says so explicitly and claims no contract. Where two independent official sources could not be obtained, the asset is recorded as unverified_identity with its evidence, or left unclassified where there is no evidence either way.
